title: Black Cat
summary: Black Cat is the user-facing brand for the Portable Trusted Linux (PTL) project. The first Debian Live hybrid ISO has been built, fingerprinted, written to USB in raw/DD mode and physically booted successfully on real hardware; that remains OBSERVED bootability only. The source includes a no-typing Black Cat System Check boot option, a controlled approved-release panel, a fail-closed public project viewer using one protected read-only GitHub token file outside the web root, and a corrected UEFI/QEMU smoke harness. The integrated replacement smoke execution remains an evidence gate before a new ISO is offered for physical testing.

release.note: No Black Cat ISO is currently approved for download. Candidate GitHub Actions artifacts are intentionally not linked. After a candidate passes the required build and boot-smoke gates, one exact ISO will be deliberately promoted as a GitHub Release asset and this record will publish its filename, exact byte size, SHA-256, source commit, build run and test status.

sections.title: Branding boundary
sections.content: Black Cat is the user-facing project/product name. Portable Trusted Linux remains the technical description and PTL remains the stable internal engineering shorthand in repository paths, PTL_ variables, workflows and existing evidence identifiers.

sections.title: Current focus
sections.content: All active engineering is focused on Black Cat / Portable Trusted Linux Prototype 1. Community Compute Commons remains paused.

sections.title: Core trust chain
sections.content: Authenticated release reference -> verified USB image -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot and TCG event log -> TPM PCR evidence -> signed UKI -> authenticated dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed disposable state -> nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Controlled download channel
sections.content: The living project page does not expose arbitrary CI artifacts as downloads. Candidate images remain candidates until one exact ISO is deliberately promoted. The approved-release record must publish its filename, exact byte size, SHA-256, source commit, build run and smoke-test state before the download button is enabled. This improves operator safety but is not a substitute for future cryptographic release signing.

sections.title: Fail-closed project viewer
sections.content: The cPanel-hosted public viewer accepts the GitHub read-only credential only from /home/learning/.blackcat/github_token, outside the public web root. The enclosing directory and token file must have no group/world permission bits. There is no environment-variable, hard-coded-token or offline authoritative-cache fallback. Missing, unsafe or invalid credential/data state causes a fail-closed response and no ISO download.

sections.title: Boot-smoke harness discipline
sections.content: A VM firmware-launch failure is classified separately from an ISO failure. The integrated and standalone UEFI tests now use explicit OVMF CODE plus a matching writable VARS pflash store rather than selecting an arbitrary OVMF_CODE file through QEMU -bios. The source correction is implemented; its replacement integrated execution remains an evidence gate.

sections.title: First physical boot
sections.content: The first generated Debian Live hybrid ISO was written to USB using raw/DD image mode and successfully booted on real hardware. This is OBSERVED bootability on that configuration only; it is not evidence that Secure Boot, TPM attestation, dm-verity, firmware trust or release authenticity have passed.

sections.title: No-typing system check
sections.content: The next image includes a Black Cat - System Check boot-menu entry. It adds blackcat.check=1 and automatically runs a modular diagnostic that displays UEFI/legacy mode, Secure Boot state exposure, TPM exposure, TCG event-log exposure, dm-verity mapper state, network-link state, kernel and architecture. The screen is designed to be photographed during offline testing.

sections.title: Evidence classification
sections.content: The quick-check screen reports observations and does not become its own ultimate verifier. Individual observations remain OBSERVED/UNKNOWN/etc. until stronger cryptographic and independent verification gates are implemented.

sections.title: Verified builder toolchain
sections.content: The remote Debian 13 builder has the declared live-build, xorriso, verity, UKI, signing and TPM tooling installed. It remains a builder rather than an attestation target because the cloud VM does not expose the required UEFI/TPM interfaces.

sections.title: Build provenance
sections.content: The successful ISO workflow records intended source commit/ref separately from checked-out commit/ref. This prevents pull-request merge-checkout identity from being confused with the source revision intended for the build.

sections.title: Immediate evidence gate
sections.content: M13 is complete: the first Debian Live reference artifact was built/fingerprinted and physically booted. M13B is current: the no-typing System Check source exists and the standalone automated smoke path has passed previously; the corrected integrated live-build smoke harness must complete successfully before an exact new candidate is handed to the operator for physical menu/report testing.

sections.title: Progressive hardening
sections.content: Prototype stages may temporarily use weaker controls to prove the workflow, but every such control must document its trust assumption, compromise path, temporary justification and stronger replacement. Bootstrap credentials, the self-hosted runner, the cPanel read-only repository token and temporary live-build privilege are not final security controls; signing keys must never be placed in the viewer credential path.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons discipline
sections.content: Every meaningful session updates docs/07-lessons-learned.md and affected specifications or decisions. project_content.json is always written last.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security components
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKI, TPM 2.0 and dm-verity rather than inventing replacement primitives.

decisions.title: Independent verification is mandatory
decisions.text: The target computer cannot be the sole authority deciding that its own measurements are trustworthy.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Documents, source and the living JSON index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory output
decisions.text: Every meaningful engineering/research session records lessons before project_content.json is updated last.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 baseline is Debian 13/trixie amd64
decisions.text: Exact build-host and package versions are captured as provenance.

decisions.title: Community Compute Commons paused
decisions.text: The research remains preserved, but active implementation returns exclusively to the core trust chain until its initial acceptance gates pass.

decisions.title: Progressive hardening is mandatory
decisions.text: Temporary weaker controls may be used to make demonstrable progress only when their assumptions, weaknesses and stronger replacements are explicit. They must never be presented as final security controls.

decisions.title: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner is the initial remote execution path
decisions.text: Repository-scoped Actions jobs provide the auditable control path into the disposable build VM. Privileged operations remain explicitly separated from the unprivileged runner.

decisions.title: Build host and attestation target are separate roles
decisions.text: The DigitalOcean VM is used for building and artifact generation. UEFI measured-boot and TPM attestation claims require a separate platform that exposes those interfaces.

decisions.title: Normalize builder capability checks
decisions.text: Host preflight uses a deterministic system PATH so service-account environment differences cannot silently hide installed administrative tools.

decisions.title: Privilege only the live-build construction stage
decisions.text: Live-build preparation is unprivileged. The actual lb build operation is the current explicit privileged boundary and any passwordless permission used for Prototype 1 is temporary, documented and subject to later hardening.

decisions.title: Record source identity separately from checkout identity
decisions.text: CI manifests record intended source commit/ref separately from the temporary merge/detached checkout identity that a pull-request workflow may use.

decisions.title: Black Cat is the user-facing brand
decisions.text: Keep PTL internal engineering identifiers stable while presenting the product/project to users as Black Cat.

decisions.title: No-typing hardware diagnostics
decisions.text: Provide a dedicated Black Cat System Check boot menu entry that automatically collects modular runtime observations and presents a photograph-friendly screen.

decisions.title: Physical boot is an observation, not attestation
decisions.text: A successful USB boot proves bootability on the tested configuration only and must not be promoted to Secure Boot, TPM, dm-verity, firmware or release-authenticity assurance.

decisions.title: Approved releases are separate from CI candidates
decisions.text: The public project viewer only exposes an ISO download after one exact candidate is deliberately promoted and its filename, byte size, SHA-256, source identity and test state are recorded. This reduces operator error but does not replace future cryptographic release signing.

decisions.title: Public viewer uses one protected read-only credential file
decisions.text: The cPanel-hosted viewer accepts only /home/learning/.blackcat/github_token, outside the public web root, with private permissions. Missing or unsafe credential state fails closed; no environment, hard-coded or cache fallback is accepted. This credential is repository-read only and must never be reused as a signing trust root.

decisions.title: UEFI QEMU tests use explicit OVMF pflash state
decisions.text: Boot-smoke workflows pair a non-secboot OVMF CODE image with its matching writable VARS template through pflash drives. Firmware-launch failures remain separate from ISO-build evidence.

changelog.summary: Initial trust chain and threat model.
Established GitHub as canonical workspace and expanded documentation.
Locked Prototype 1 baseline and mandatory lessons-learned process.
Added safe first-stage build tooling and static validation.
Paused Community Compute Commons implementation, restored exclusive focus to core Prototype 1, and added the single-command first real-builder evidence collector.
Provisioned the first remote Debian 13 builder and formalized weak-to-strong progressive hardening as a mandatory project rule.
Established the self-hosted GitHub Actions execution path, completed the first real-builder evidence run, and separated the cloud build-host role from later UEFI/TPM attestation testing.
Verified the builder toolchain, fixed the runner PATH false negative and live-build directory mismatch, and advanced to the first ISO build milestone.

Rebranded the user-facing project as Black Cat while retaining PTL internals, recorded the first successful physical USB boot, and added a no-typing System Check boot path for real-hardware diagnostics.

Added a controlled approved-ISO download panel so CI candidates cannot be mistaken for the test image intended for users; the button remains disabled until an exact release is explicitly promoted with size, SHA-256, source and smoke-test metadata.

Hardened the public project viewer to fail closed by removing embedded/fallback credentials and stale authoritative release data; approved downloads additionally require a valid source commit plus a passed smoke test.

Synchronized the public viewer with its working single protected token-file deployment and corrected the integrated QEMU UEFI smoke harness to use explicit OVMF CODE/VARS pflash state; the replacement integrated run remains an evidence gate before physical testing.
